title: Existence of normalized section scalar comparisons
statement: For every morphism a of commutative condensed rings and every scheme T, there exists a SectionScalarComparison a T satisfying SectionScalarNormalized. The comparison structures and all normalization equations are exactly those of [def-sfb-internal-section-scalar-pullback-comparison-data], using the scalar functor and counit of [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons]. No flatness assumption on a is imposed.

source.place: Paragraph (1), reduction comparison in the specified coefficient category; extracted old step 2. Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint).

proof.text: Apply internal_section_scalar_adjunction to the pulled-back coefficient map. Retain its section scalar pair, identity-on-sections restriction comparison, balanced ordinary extension comparison, and the derived comparison normalized on flat-term K-flat representatives.

Use exists_homotopy_leftDerived_comparison to transport the universal internal cochain counit to the homotopy quotient. The fixed scalar functor D is another universal left-derived functor of the same ordinary extension. The canonical leftDerivedNatIso between them has its defining counit equation. The quotient and complex-factor comparison maps are identities on these objects, so that equation identifies its component with compute. Whisker the isomorphism by the exact section equivalence and compose with the supplied derived extension comparison. Functoriality, associativity and the supplied representative square give SectionScalarNormalized; the ordinary clauses were unchanged.
